post.caption: A curtain ring made a duchess. By 1750, crowds followed the Gunning sisters around London. Horace Walpole wrote that the Duke of Hamilton fell for Elizabeth. The Duke sent for a clergyman. The clergyman refused, because there was no license and no ring. The Duke swore he would fetch the Archbishop. In Walpole's account, they married with a ring off the bed curtain. It was half an hour after midnight, in a Mayfair chapel. A new marriage law ended such weddings in 1754. The register dates the wedding February 14, 1752, Valentine's Day.
